mainTopic: The proof for שמואל from a found כתובה receipt, and a new משנה about returning found court documents and bundles of documents
overview: The גמרא finishes a discussion about a found receipt for a כתובה. Since we do not worry that the wife secretly sold her כתובה, the גמרא suggests this proves שמואל's rule that a seller of a loan document can still cancel the debt. אביי rejects the proof: the wife may still hold the כתובה document, so there was no sale. רבא objects that maybe there were two copies of the כתובה. אביי answers that we do not worry about two copies, and that a receipt works from the date written on it, which fits his view that signing witnesses acquire a document for its owner. A new משנה then lists court documents a finder must return, rules on bundles of documents and who gets them back, and says a document of unknown status is left alone. The גמרא explains שטרי בירורין in two ways and begins a story about a גט found in רב הונא's court, whose ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to prove שמואל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא does not worry that the wife sold her כתובה, the גמרא concludes this supports שמואל: someone who sells a loan document can still cancel the debt, and so can his heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that we follow שמואל. שמואל said: if someone sells a loan document to another person and then cancels the debt, it is cancelled. Even the seller's heir can cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the case just discussed: since we do not worry that the wife sold her כתובה, we must accept שמואל's rule that a seller can still cancel a debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the wife sold her כתובה to someone else and is now working with her husband to cheat the buyer with a receipt. If the seller of a debt can always cancel it anyway, as שמואל says, then there is nothing to worry about, because she was allowed to cancel it. So the lack of worry looks like proof for שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude

steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule is a basic principle in the laws of selling debts: the buyer of a loan document is never fully safe, because the original lender can still cancel the debt.

phrases.english: Learn from this: the ruling of Shmuel is accepted,
phrases.notes: Since we didn't worry that she sold her כתובה, the גמרא assumes it's because she could cancel it anyway.

phrases.english: as Shmuel said:
One who sells a loan document to another,
and then went back and forgave the debt – it is forgiven,
and even an heir can forgive it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the earlier ruling about a found כתובה receipt, where we did not worry that the wife sold her כתובה.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling of שמואל that a seller of a loan document can still cancel the debt
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that we return a found כתובה receipt without worrying that the wife sold her כתובה

steps.title: אביי: the case is where she still holds the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. Even without שמואל, the case may be one where the כתובה document itself comes out of the wife's possession, which shows she never sold it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: even if you say we do not follow שמואל, here we are dealing with a case where the כתובה document comes out from her possession.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof. He says there is a different reason we do not worry: in this case the wife still has her כתובה document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she had sold the כתובה, the buyer would be holding the document. Since she still holds it, there was clearly no sale, so there is nothing to worry about. That means the case proves nothing about שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even if you say Shmuel's ruling is not accepted,
here, what are we dealing with?
A case where the marriage contract document comes out from her possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא לֵיתַיהּ לְדִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for שמואל by explaining the case differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only; אביי does not say שמואל is wrong, only that this case does not prove him right.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lack of worry can be explained because she still holds the כתובה document, not because of שמואל's rule.

steps.title: רבא: maybe there were two כתובה documents
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to אביי: holding the כתובה document is not enough, because we should worry she had two copies and sold one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if the reason is because she holds the כתובה document, we should worry that there are two כתובה documents.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's answer. He says the fact that she holds a כתובה document does not prove she never sold one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe two copies of the כתובה were written. She could have sold one copy and kept the other. If so, the document in her hand proves nothing.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
If the reason is because of the marriage contract document,
we should worry about two marriage contracts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: אִי מִשּׁוּם שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that holding the כתובה document shows she did not sell it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There may have been two copies; she could have sold one and kept the other.

steps.title: אביי answers: no worry of two כתובות, and the receipt works from its date
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives two answers: first, we do not worry about two כתובה documents; second, even if she sold it, a receipt collects from the date written on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: first, we do not worry about two כתובה documents. And also, a receipt can collect from its date.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his position with two separate answers to רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, two copies of a כתובה is too unlikely to worry about. Second, even if she did sell it, the receipt takes effect from the date written on it, even if it was handed over later. So a sale made after that date cannot hurt the husband.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt showing a debt was paid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the receipt only works from the day it was handed over. אביי says it works from the date written on it.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: first,
we do not worry about two marriage contracts.
And furthermore, a receipt collects from its date.
phrases.notes: The receipt counts from the date written on it, even if she sold the כתובה before she gave the receipt to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּיֵי אָמַר, חֲדָא: לִשְׁתֵּי כְתוּבּוֹת לָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two answers: rejects the worry, and adds a legal rule that removes the problem anyway
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A second copy of the כתובה could have been sold, so her holding a copy proves nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two copies are too unlikely to worry about, and in any case the receipt works from its written date.

steps.title: אביי is consistent: witnesses acquire for him by signing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי's second answer fits his known view that the witnesses' signatures acquire the document for its owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי follows his own reasoning, because he said: the witnesses, by signing, acquire the document for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where אביי's second answer comes from: his general rule about signed documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once witnesses sign a document, it already belongs to the person it was written for, even before he receives it. That is why the receipt counts from its date.

keyTerms.meaning: The witnesses, by signing, acquire the document for him

steps.whatToRemember: אביי rejects the proof for שמואל: we don't worry about two כתובות, and by his rule that witnesses acquire for the owner by signing, a receipt works from its date.

phrases.english: Abaye follows his own reasoning, as he said:
Its witnesses, through their signatures, acquire it for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source of אביי's second answer in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אביי, the signing witnesses acquire a document for its owner, so it takes effect from the date written.

steps.title: New משנה: court documents a finder must return
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists documents connected to בית דין that a finder must give back: property appraisals, food support, חליצה, מיאון, בירורין, and any court action.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone found documents of appraisal, documents about food support, documents of חליצה or מיאון, documents of בירורין, or any court document, he must return them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists found documents that the finder must return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of these documents come from בית דין or court-related matters, and the משנה rules that the finder must return each of them. The גמרא explains the term בירורין in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה; the start of a new משנה
Documents of property appraisal for debt collection
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
Refusals of a girl married as a minor

phrases.english: MISHNA: If one found documents of appraisal
or documents of food support,
documents of halitza or refusal,
or documents of beirurin,
phrases.notes: The גמרא will explain what בירורין are a little later.

phrases.english: or any court action,
he must return it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מָצָא אִיגְּרוֹת שׁוּם וְאִיגְּרוֹת מָזוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A finder must return court-related documents such as appraisals, food support documents, חליצה and מיאון documents, בירורין, and any court action.

steps.title: Documents found in a container or bundle must be returned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that documents found in a container, a roll, or a bundle must be returned, and defines a bundle as three documents tied together.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone finds documents in a חפיסה or a דלוסקמא (types of containers), or finds a roll of documents or a bundle of documents, he must return them. How many make a bundle? Three tied together.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case: documents found together in a container or tied in a bundle must be returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loose single documents may be hard to identify, but here the container or the bundle gives the owner a way to describe what he lost. The משנה also sets a minimum: a bundle means at least three documents tied together.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of bag or container
A kind of box or case

phrases.english: If he found documents in a chafisa or in a deluskema,
phrases.notes: Both words are names of containers, like a bag or a case.

phrases.english: or a roll of documents
or a bundle of documents –
he must return them.
And how many make a bundle of documents?
Three that are tied to each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of found documents with a new case of grouped documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Documents found in a container, roll, or bundle (three tied together) must be returned.

steps.title: Who gets the bundle back: borrower or lender
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that the bundle goes to whichever person is common to all the documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if the documents show one person who borrowed from three, return them to the borrower. If they show three people who borrowed from one, return them to the lender.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל tells us to whom the found bundle should be returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person who appears in every document is most likely the one who had them all together and lost them. So if one borrower is in all of them, they go to him; if one lender is in all of them, they go to him.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If one person borrowed from three –
he returns them to the borrower.
If three people borrowed from one –
he returns them to the lender.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule about who receives the bundle that the previous step said must be returned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Return the bundle to the person common to all the documents: the single borrower or the single lender.

steps.title: A document of unknown status stays put
steps.stepSummary: If a person finds a document among his own papers and does not know its status, it is left alone unless cancellation notes tell him what to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found a document among his documents and does not know what its status is, it should be left until אליהו comes. If there are סימפונות with them, he should do what the סימפונות say.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case: a person holding papers for others finds one whose status he cannot figure out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he cannot tell whose it is or whether the debt was paid, he may not give it to either side. It stays put until the truth is known, unless a סימפון (a note cancelling or explaining it) is found with it, which settles the matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Until אליהו comes: left until the truth is revealed
Notes that cancel or explain a document, like receipts

phrases.english: If he found a document among his documents
phrases.notes: These are papers other people gave him to hold.

phrases.english: and he does not know what its status is –
it should be left until Eliyahu comes.
If there are simponot with them,
he should do what is in the simponot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the משנה, moving from found bundles to a document of unclear status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A document of unknown status is left untouched unless סימפונות show what to do with it.
steps.whatToRemember: When you cannot tell who a document belongs to or whether it was paid, you do nothing with it until clear evidence appears.

steps.title: What are documents of בירורין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה meant by שטרי בירורין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the meaning of a term from the earlier משנה. This sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 listed שטרי בירורין among court documents a finder must return, but did not explain the term. The גמרא wants to know exactly what kind of document this is.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and explains the משנה
Documents of בירורין: the term being explained

phrases.english: GEMARA
What are "documents of beirurin"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a term from the משנה in step 6 to clarify it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the term שטרי בירורין.

steps.title: Two explanations of בירורין
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they explain it as documents of claims; רבי ירמיה explains it as documents recording each side's chosen judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they explained it as documents of claims. רבי ירמיה said: this one chooses one judge and that one chooses one judge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different answers to what שטרי בירורין means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view: they are papers where each side writes down his claims in the case. רבי ירמיה: they are papers recording which judge each side picked, since each side chooses one judge for the court.

keyTerms.meaning: Documents of claims: each side's arguments written down

phrases.english: Here they explained it as documents of claims.
phrases.notes: "Here" means in בבל, as opposed to רבי ירמיה from ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
This one chooses one judge for himself
and that one chooses one judge for himself.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either documents of each side's claims, or (רבי ירמיה) documents recording each side's chosen judge.

steps.title: A divorce document found in רב הונא's court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about any court action and begins a story of a גט found in רב הונא's court.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And any court action, he must return it." There was a גט found in the court of רב הונא, in which was written "in Sheviri city, which is on the Rakhis river." רב הונא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the משנה's phrase about any court action and starts telling a story. This is a setup: רב הונא's ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story tests the rule from step 6 with a real case: a found גט naming a specific place. The detail of the town and river is given because it will matter for what רב הונא decides.

keyTerms.meaning: Any court action or court document
An אמורא who headed a court

phrases.english: "And any court action"
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the end of the משנה's list from step 6.

phrases.english: "he must return it."
There was a certain divorce document that was found
in the court of Rav Huna,
in which was written
"In Sheviri city
which is on the Rakhis river."
Rav Huna said:

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גִּיטָּא דְּאִשְׁתְּכַח בֵּי דִינָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining בירורין to the next phrase of the משנה, introducing a case story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a case of a found גט naming a specific town; רב הונא's ruling follows.
